gender.label: female

year.evidence: I’m in the third year and you get to decide basically what you want to do in third year

answer_quotes: I wasn’t going to do it for years and then I applied for loads of courses and then realised that the only thing I wanted to do was music, so I had to come here to do it because they can’t do it in Ireland. So I said yeah, because I knew if I did something else I’d regret not doing music.
the critical side I like a lot and also the producing side, so I came in wanting to be a producer but that’s slightly changed a bit, I don’t really know what I want to do anymore.

I was taught music from a young age anyway, so I didn’t really, well, I had a choice, but I was going to learn music whatever and then, yeah, so they’ve had – they have had an influence on it because they’re both musicians.

I kind of had an idea of what you could go into, like sound engineering and producing and stuff like that, but I suppose you don’t realise, well, with music how little work there is really until you come to university.

I just applied to a few universities and – for music technology because not that many places do it, um, and these were the first people to send me a letter to come for an open day, so I came here first

there was a lot of stuff involved in the degree that we weren’t made aware of before we went in, like a lot of multimedia, um, stuff that we – that nobody really wanted to do in the course, but we’ve done it now
the best things are working in the studio with other musicians on the performance side of things. Um, I love critical studies as well, which is just talking about music and arguing about it

The worst, um, doing a lot of multimedia that I knew I would never want to do again. That I’d never – I wouldn’t use it again and I would never think about a career in that field but yet I still had to do it to pass.
we’ve a group project this year which is, um, a third of our whole degree, which we think is far too much because you’re relying on a lot of other people for a third of your degree.
I think if I’d known how much multimedia was involved in this I might have chosen a different course, but I’m still glad that I did it.

the placements they were offering us were completely nothing to do with our side of things. It was, um, it was basically a factory work that had small relation to electronics somewhere, but nothing to do with music or anything like that. So everyone – a lot of people didn’t do it.

If there had been something which really interests me I think probably yeah, but the other thing was the cost, that we still had to pay for being in the University even though we’d be out working, and that put a lot of people off.
And the fact that they’d probably have to move to London or somewhere like that, so it’d be more expensive.
I think experience is probably more important than a degree when it comes to my – music technology, but I just wanted to do the degree anyway. But, um, the experience is very important.
I’d like to get into the business – the business side of things somehow, the industry side of things. But where I’ll start I don’t really know. I haven’t got a clue.
I’d like to run my own thing eventually, to be able to make my own music and I’d like to do my own business side of things as well, but mainly just being able to make music, yeah.
I think salary, I mean it is important but it’s not what I’m going to look for. That’ll just be a bonus if it happens to be good
Yeah, travel for a couple of months and then work. Um, and I don’t know what kind of work I’m looking for. I think I’ll probably just work wherever and then think about a career when I come back here
the money side of things because it’s going to take a long time to start earning money and then paying back debts and stuff like that. It’s going to be for a couple of years really hard to cope with
